title: useGetSwitchboardLink returns null for local drives and mints a fresh bearer token per call
content:
`useGetSwitchboardLink` is the hook behind the toolbar's Switchboard button, and its signature encodes a precondition:

```ts
function useGetSwitchboardLink(
  document: PHDocument | undefined,
): (() => Promise<string>) | null;
```

It returns `null` — not a function that fails — when there is nothing to link to. Callers branch on the null and hide their button entirely.

"Remote" is not a flag on the drive. The hook takes the selected drive, builds `DriveCollectionId.forDrive(drive.header.id)`, and looks for a matching entry in `useSyncList()`. A drive is remote precisely when a sync remote exists for its collection id. The endpoint then comes from that remote's channel config (`(remote.channel as GqlRequestChannel).config.url`), so a purely local drive with no configured remote yields `null` even though the document is perfectly real. Three things must all resolve — a remote drive, a document id, and a remote URL — or the hook returns `null`.

The token is minted at **call** time, not render time. Inside the returned async function:

```ts
const token = user?.address
  ? await renown?.getBearerToken({ expiresIn: 600, aud: remoteUrl })
  : undefined;
return buildDocumentSubgraphUrl(remoteUrl, document.header.id, token);
```

Two consequences. First, the credential has a 600-second (10-minute) lifetime and is audienced to the specific remote URL, so a link generated now cannot be pasted into a chat and opened tomorrow, and cannot be replayed against a different Switchboard. Second, when no Renown user address is present the token is simply `undefined` and the URL is built anonymously rather than the call failing — so an unauthenticated user gets a link that may be rejected at the far end.

Because the function is async, wire it to a handler that awaits the URL and then opens it, rather than putting it in an `href`.

_Source: packages/reactor-browser/src/hooks/use-get-switchboard-link.ts, documented at apps/academy/docs/academy/04-Reference/05-EditorsUI/01-ReactHooks.md (Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45)._
description: The hook returns an async URL generator only for documents in remote drives; each call mints a 10-minute bearer token audienced to the remote and builds an authenticated Switchboard URL.
